title: The logarithm on sufficiently deep principal units
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_E$, and normalized valuation
$v_E(\mathfrak m_E)=1$. If $e=v_E(\ell)$, then for every integer

$$
r>\frac{e}{\ell-1}
$$

the power series

$$
\log(1+x)=\sum_{n\geq1}(-1)^{n+1}\frac{x^n}{n},
\exp(x)=\sum_{n\geq0}\frac{x^n}{n!}
$$

converge on $\mathfrak m_E^r$, are inverse there, and give mutually
inverse continuous group homomorphisms

$$
\log:1+\mathfrak m_E^r\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak m_E^r,
\qquad
\exp:\mathfrak m_E^r\xrightarrow{\sim}1+\mathfrak m_E^r.
$$

Moreover, there is an integer $N\geq1$ such that
$u^N\in1+\mathfrak m_E^r$ for every $u\in\mathcal O_E^\times$.

proof.text: Put $I=\mathfrak m_E^r$, $q=\ell^{-r/e}$ and $\delta=r-e/(\ell-1)>0$. Write $L(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{n+1}T^n/n$ and $A(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}T^n/n!$, so the desired maps are $u\mapsto L(u-1)$ and $x\mapsto1+A(x)$. By [lem-wf-log-exp-valuation-convergence], $L,A$ converge uniformly on $I=\{|x|_E\le q\}$, have continuous sums in $I$, and each of their weighted coefficient sequences at radius $q$ is bounded by $q\theta^{n-1}\to0$, where $\theta=\ell^{-\delta/e}<1$. In particular both weighted coefficient suprema are at most $q$.

source.place: paragraphs 1–2 and the coefficient bounds needed by paragraph 3

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-wf-nonarchimedean-series-substitution] twice, with $\rho=s=q$, first $(F,G)=(L,A)$ and then $(F,G)=(A,L)$. Both inner series have zero constant term; step 1 supplies restrictedness, the bound $\sup_m|b_m|_Eq^m\le q$, and $|a_n|_Eq^n\to0$ in each case. For either pair, an expanded term $a_n\prod_{j=1}^n b_{m_j}x^{m_j}$ has norm at most $|a_n|_Eq^n\le q\theta^{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$. This bound tends to zero with $n$, and for fixed $n$ the terms tend to zero as the tuple escapes finite subsets, by the inner coefficient decay. Thus the cited criterion makes the full expanded composition families summable. The formal identities [lem-wf-log-exp-formal-identities], specialized to the commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra $E$, can therefore be evaluated to give $L(A(x))=x$ and $A(L(x))=x$ for every $x\in I$. Consequently $\log(\exp x)=x$ and $\exp(\log(1+x))=1+x$.

source.place: paragraph 3, inverse identities with explicit summability hypotheses

proof.text:
Fix $a,b\in I$; then $a+b\in I$ by the nonarchimedean inequality. Apply [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] with $R=E$, $U=aT$ and $W=bT$. These have zero constant coefficients, and its formal identity is
$$\left(\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{a^nT^n}{n!}\right)\left(\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{b^nT^n}{n!}\right)=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{(a+b)^nT^n}{n!}.$$
By [lem-wf-log-exp-valuation-convergence], the coefficient sequences of all three series tend to zero: their positive-degree terms have norms at most $q\theta^{n-1}$. They are therefore restricted at radius $1$. Clause (1) of [lem-wf-nonarchimedean-series-substitution] permits evaluating this Cauchy product at $T=1$ (whose norm is $1$), giving $\exp(a+b)=\exp(a)\exp(b)$. This works simultaneously for every pair $a,b$ and does not substitute $x+y+xy$ into a one-variable identity.

source.place: paragraph 3, homomorphism identity via formal exponential addition and a summable Cauchy product

proof.text: The two inverse identities of step 2 identify $I$ bijectively with $1+I$. Also $\exp(0)=1$ directly from the series. Step 3 gives $\exp(a)\exp(-a)=1$, so all these values are units, and proves multiplicative closure and the homomorphism property of exponential. For $u,v\in1+I$, put $a=\log u$, $b=\log v$. Step 2 gives $u=\exp a$, $v=\exp b$, so step 3 and then step 2 give $\log(uv)=\log(\exp(a+b))=a+b$. Thus logarithm is the inverse homomorphism. Continuity of both maps follows from [lem-wf-log-exp-valuation-convergence], with the translations $u\mapsto u-1$ and $x\mapsto1+x$ continuous in the field topology. This proves all the asserted topological group claims.

For the finite extension with its extended absolute value [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], clauses 2–4 of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] give that $\mathcal O_E$ is a DVR with finite residue field and a uniformizer $\varpi$. Since $r>e/(\ell-1)>0$, the integer $r$ is at least $1$. Clauses 1–2 of [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] identify $\varpi^r\mathcal O_E=\mathfrak m_E^r$ and make $\mathcal O_E/\mathfrak m_E^r$ finite. Reduction maps $\mathcal O_E^\times$ to the unit group of that finite ring. A unit maps to $1$ exactly when $u-1\in\mathfrak m_E^r$, so its kernel is $1+\mathfrak m_E^r$. Taking $N\ge1$ to be the exponent of the finite image yields $u^N\in1+\mathfrak m_E^r$ for every unit $u$.
